'''Dame Charmian Jocelyn O'Connor''' {{post-nominals|country=NZL|DNZM|CBE|JP}} (née '''Bishop''', born 4 August 1937) is a New Zealand [[Physical organic chemistry|physical organic chemist]].  She became the first female professor of chemistry at the [[University of Auckland]] in 1986, and retired in 2004.

==Early life and education==
Born in [[Woodville, New Zealand|Woodville]] on 4 August 1937, the daughter of Cecil and Kathrene Bishop, O'Connor was educated at [[Hastings Girls' High School|Hastings High School]] and [[Auckland Girls' Grammar School]].<ref name="Whos who">{{cite book |editor-last=Taylor |editor-first=Alister |editor-link=Alister Taylor |title=New Zealand Who's Who Aotearoa 2001 |year=2001 |publisher=Alister Taylor Publishers |location=Auckland |issn=1172-9813 |page=672}}</ref> She went on to study chemistry at [[University of Auckland|Auckland University College]], graduating [[Bachelor of Science]] in 1957, [[Master of Science]] with first-class honours in 1958, and completing a [[PhD]] in physical organic chemistry in 1963 at what by that time had become the University of Auckland.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref name="Suffrage 125">{{cite web |url=http://suffrage125science.auckland.ac.nz |title=Suffrage 125 – women in science |year=2018 |publisher=University of Auckland |accessdate=30 September 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://shadowsoftime.co.nz/university3.html |title=NZ university graduates 1870–1961: Bh–Bre |website=Shadows of Time |accessdate=30 September 2018}}</ref>

==Academic and research career==
O'Connor was appointed as a lecturer in chemistry at Auckland University College in 1958, rising to the rank of professor in 1986, becoming Auckland's first female professor of chemistry.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/> When she retired in 2004, O'Connor was conferred the title of [[Emeritus#In academia|professor emeritus]] by the University of Auckland.<ref name="Calendar">{{cite web |url=https://www.calendar.auckland.ac.nz/en/university-personnel/professores-emeriti.html |title=Professores emeriti |year=2018 |publisher=University of Auckland |accessdate=1 October 2018}}</ref>

O'Connor has also held visiting positions at several other universities. In 1963, she took leave from Auckland to be a [[postdoctoral researcher]] at [[University College London]], having been awarded a fellowship by New Zealand [[Federation of University Women]],<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|first=Charmian | last=O'Connor|title=Some Personal Reminiscences of 54 Years in Chemistry at The University of Auckland|journal=Chemistry in New Zealand|volume=71|issue=2|date=July 2007|url=https://nzic.org.nz/unsecure_files/cinz/2007-71-2.pdf|publisher=[[New Zealand Institute of Chemistry]]|pages=43-46|issn=0110-5566}}</ref> which also paid for her research trip to [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in the same year. She returned to London in 1972, this time for a post at [[Imperial College London|Imperial College]], where she worked with future [[List of Nobel laureates in Chemistry|Nobel laureate]] [[Geoffrey Wilkinson]],<ref name=":2">{{Cite journal|title=Honours awarded to chemists|journal=Chemistry in New Zealand|volume=53|issue=4|date=August 1989|url=https://nzic.org.nz/unsecure_files/cinz/1989-53-4.pdf|publisher=[[New Zealand Institute of Chemistry]]|pages=66-67|issn=0110-5566}}</ref> supported by a grant from the [[Canadian Federation of University Women]]. The same year, she received a [[Fulbright Program|Fulbright]] grant for a visiting position at [[Texas A&M University]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Fitzgerald |first=Tanya |last2=Kirkby |first2=Diane |last3=Jordan |first3=Caroline |date=2024-07-03 |title=Lines of Exchange: Australian and New Zealand Women on Carnegie and Fulbright Programme Awards c. 1930s–1980s |url=https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/0046760X.2024.2333953 |journal=History of Education |language=en |volume=53 |issue=4 |pages=685–705 |doi=10.1080/0046760X.2024.2333953 |issn=0046-760X |doi-access=free}}</ref> O'Connor also held visiting professorships at Universities of [[Nagasaki University|Nagasaki]] and [[University of Tokushima|Tokushima]] in Japan.<ref name=":2" /> 

O'Connor authored or co-authored more than 300 scientific papers in refereed journals.<ref name="Kate Edger">{{cite web |url=https://www.academicdresshire.co.nz/About%2BUs/The%2BKate%2BEdger%2BEducational%2BCharitable%2BTrust.html |title=Kate Edger Educational Charitable Trust |date= |website=Academic Dress Hire |accessdate=1 October 2018}}</ref> Her research focused on the [[Reaction mechanism|mechanisms]] and [[Chemical kinetics|kinetics]] of reactions involving [[biologically active]] compounds.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://royalsociety.org.nz/who-we-are/our-people/our-fellows/view-our-fellows/ |title=List of fellows of the Royal Society of New Zealand |year=2018 |publisher=Royal Society of New Zealand |accessdate=1 October 2018}}</ref> In 1973, she was conferred the degree of [[Doctor of Science]] (DSc) by the University of Auckland on the basis of published papers submitted, becoming the first woman in New Zealand to be awarded a DSc.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/><ref>{{cite web |url=https://catalogue.library.auckland.ac.nz/primo-explore/fulldisplay?docid=uoa_alma21184134970002091&context=L&vid=NEWUI&search_scope=Combined_Local&tab=books&lang=en_US |title=Library catalogue search |publisher=University of Auckland |accessdate=1 October 2018}}</ref>

During her career at Auckland, O'Connor held many administrative roles at the university, including serving as the inaugural assistant vice-chancellor, equal employment opportunities and staff development, from 1987 to 1998, and deputy vice-chancellor in 1994.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/><ref name="Kate Edger"/>

==Other activities==
O'Connor served as a member of the Ministerial Advisory Group for science and technology, and on the national commission for UNESCO.<ref name="Whos who"/> Between 1979 and 1981, she was the national president of the New Zealand Federation of University Women.<ref name="Whos who" /> In 2005, she founded the Kate Edger Foundation, which awards upwards of {{Currency|600,000|NZD}} in scholarships and fellowships to women annually.<ref name=":0" /> A Master’s Degree in Science scholarship of {{Currency|8000|NZD}} is awarded annually by the foundation in O'Connor's honour.<ref>{{Cite web |title=All Awards and Scholarships |url=https://kateedgerfoundation.org.nz/award_list/all-awards-awards-list/ |access-date=2026-04-17 |website=The Kate Edger Foundation |language=en-NZ}}</ref> She served as the foundation's chair of trustee board for nine years from its establishment<ref name="Kate Edger" /> and remained as a trustee until 2021.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Yeats |first=Jodi |date=4 November 2021 |title=Dame Charmian O'Connor: a force in women's education |url=https://www.auckland.ac.nz/en/news/2021/11/04/a-force-in-women-s-education.html |access-date=2026-04-17 |website=[[University of Auckland]]}}</ref>

O'Connor served on the councils of a number of educational institutions, including the [[Manukau Institute of Technology]], [[Unitec Institute of Technology]], and the [[Diocesan School for Girls, Auckland|Diocesan School for Girls]].<ref name="Whos who" />

Between 1961 and 1962, O'Connor was the secretary of the Auckland branch of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry, and was later a member of the Academy Council of the [[Royal Society of New Zealand]].<ref name="Whos who"/>

In 1982, O'Connor was appointed as a [[justice of the peace]].<ref name="Whos who"/>

==Honours and awards==
In the [[1989 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|1989 Queen's Birthday Honours]], O'Connor was appointed a [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]], for services to chemistry, education and the community.<ref>{{London Gazette |issue=51774 |date=17 June 1989 |supp=3 |page=32}}</ref> She became a [[Dame Companion of the New Zealand Order of Merit]], for services to chemistry and education, in the [[2018 Birthday Honours (New Zealand)|2018 Queen's Birthday Honours]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dpmc.govt.nz/publications/queens-birthday-honours-list-2018 |title=Queen's Birthday honours list 2018 |date=4 June 2018 |publisher=Department of the Prime Minister and Cabinet |accessdate=1 October 2018}}</ref>
 
O'Connor was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of New Zealand]] in 1986,<ref name="Suffrage 125"/> and is also a [[Fellow of the Royal Society of Chemistry]] and a Fellow of the New Zealand Institute of Chemistry.<ref name="Whos who"/><ref name="Calendar"/>

In 2018, during the celebrations to mark 125 years of women's suffrage in New Zealand, the science faculty at the University of Auckland was temporarily renamed the Dame Charmian O'Connor Faculty of Science in honour of O'Connor's contribution to science.<ref name="Suffrage 125"/>
==Personal life==
In 1963, she married Peter Selwyn O'Connor and took on his surname. The couple have a son and a daughter.<ref name="NNZ">{{cite book |title=Notable New Zealanders |page=349 |publisher=Paul Hamblyn |location=Auckland |year=1979 |editor-last=Jackson |editor-first=Desney |ISBN=086832020X}}</ref><ref name=":1" />
